analysis.title: Marketcolour + HF Update, Midterms / Europe Conviction List / Alstom / Ryanair / LVMH / Nicotine
key_insights: US equities fell on the week: SPX -182 bps to 7580, NDX -346 bps to 28384 (about a 7% move in October), RTY -166 bps to 2811. Nasdaq had its worst session since June and second-worst YTD, with the Tech sector -4.24%. Energy (+1.91%) and Consumer Staples (+1.38%) were up.

The AI trade took the biggest hit: GS AI Semis basket (GSCBSMHX) -8.25% on the week and GS Data Center basket (GSTMTDAT) -7.35%. In Europe, EU High Beta Momentum (GSPEMOMO) -2.8% and EU Beta (GSP3BETA) -2.5%, while the EU Stagflation pair (GSPESTAG) +2% was among the best baskets.

October moves: NDX vs Equal Weight S&P had its worst month since 2002, SOX broke below its 200-day moving average for the first time since June 2025, and Software vs Semis had its second-best month in 10 years. AI vs 'AI at Risk' had its second-worst month since ChatGPT launched, while S&P ex-AI had its strongest month (+7.64%).

Hedge fund performance: Fundamental LS managers up 0.3% on the week (alpha +0.1%), with gains Monday to Thursday partly erased Friday. Alpha came from stock selection and Health Care, partly offset by Brazil exposure. Communication Services and Info Tech were the most net bought sectors, with Info Tech net bought for the first time in 5 weeks. October: Fundamental LS down 3.5% (alpha -1.8%). YTD: up 9.1% (alpha +6.6%).

Flow: Asset managers finished net sellers, reversing early-week tech demand, while HF flows were balanced. Most supply was in tech, but orderly compared with the prior ~2 weeks. Moves looked systematic / top-down, with ETFs about 31% of tape (highest full-session level since June). Month-end dynamics also contributed.

In a Democratic sweep scenario, GS's favorite long basket is Affordable Care Act Beneficiaries (GSHLCACA), because reviving the enhanced ACA premium tax credits that expired at end-2025 should improve earnings for hospitals, outpatient providers and health insurers facing rising bad debt and uncompensated care costs.

US midterms: prediction markets imply >90% odds Democrats win the House and >65% the Senate. Legislative focus under a Democratic majority would be fiscal deadlines (spending authority extension, debt limit increase). GS does not expect major fiscal policy changes over the next 2 years, but spending could increase.
Europe Conviction List: Deutsche Bank and Carlsberg added; HSBC, Haleon and CTP removed.

US Strategy: Q3 2026 earnings growth is strong but no longer accelerating. Analysts continued to raise forward estimates but the rate of upward revisions slowed. GS view is that AI capex will keep growing but the growth rate is peaking.

Alstom cut 2026 guidance: growth to low-to-mid single digit (vs 5% previously), adjusted EBIT margin 1% (vs 6.5%), FCF -EUR1.5bn (vs positive). The cause is primarily Coradia Max milestones slipping into later years, plus prolonged Middle East uncertainty. The company says the Coradia Max issues were first identified in Q1.

Ryanair H1 initial take is OK: Q2 PAT in line, Q3 fares trending modestly higher y/y, and a new EUR800m buyback starting February signals confidence. FY28 fuel is only 25% hedged (up from 15%), a headwind into next year.

European nicotine: GS upgrades BAT to Buy (22% upside) and keeps Imperial at Buy (22% upside). Both offer double-digit total returns, with robust earnings growth, rising capital returns and about 6% dividend yields. GS sees nicotine's defensive qualities and margins as attractive into FY27.

LVMH (Buy, PT EUR495, 25% upside): GS argues the shift from a commercial, fashion-driven brand to a handbag and accessories-focused strategy around the 'art of travel' has weighed on sales over the last twelve months and should be a much smaller headwind in 2027. Dior shows evidence of gradual sales improvement.
Unilever: GS published 10 investor debates ahead of the Unilever capital markets day.

Mag7 positioning has been very resilient despite the volatile TMT tape, moving from under-owned in June to near YTD highs in exposure. GS expects the group to act as a source of funds, limiting near-term dip-buying demand.
HF pain: GS's HF VIP vs VIP Short basket had its third-worst month in 15 years. GS says P&L protection over P&L generation will limit offense in the near term.
